owner_declarations: The estate owner owns all data in the estate and has declared every right to use it established (owner statement, 2 October 2026). Rights are therefore settled facts, not open questions, and no recommendation is conditional on them.
Personal-data markers remain a measured condition of the rows: de-identification or aggregation is a preparation step for a product, not a rights question.
constraints.report_scope: Lead with answers. The whole-estate figures (F130 onward) are Monte Carlo forecasts that scale the read sample to every listed folder, refused and unsampled stores included; state them as the estate's most likely holdings with their 95 % forecast interval, and say plainly which share rests on direct measurement. Access limits, restorations and unfinished samples belong in the preparation chapter and the risks, stated once as the work that converts forecast into measurement — never as the headline and never as a reason to withhold an estimate. Keep measured and forecast figures distinguishable. Forecast intervals carry sampling and between-folder variation, not model error. Storage-class percentages apply only to the class-observed subset; legacy full-Standard-price scenarios are not verified net savings.

outputs.role: model workbook: inputs, options, series and cross-checks

purpose.statement: Give the estate owner one executive, estate-wide account from census eij-1b359b3cbd2e that leads with the answer: what the whole RMS estate holds (hours, speech, music, languages and bytes, forecast for every listed folder with its interval), its strongest assets, where value concentrates, what preparation it needs, which paths earn or save money first, and what management is asked to decide.
